text: CARS (Compensatory Anti-Inflammatory Response Syndrome), proposed by Roger Bone (1997), describes counter-regulatory mechanisms limiting overzealous inflammation in sepsis/SIRS, potentially raising ICU susceptibility to nosocomial infections (per animal 'two-hit' models, procedure-dependent). Circulating leukocytes are reprogrammed, not globally defective; tissue leukocytes are primed/activated rather than immunosuppressed—an adapted, compartmentalized response silencing acute proinflammatory genes while preserving anti-infectious ones. Separately, CAR-redirected Tregs targeting lung epithelia in mouse allergic asthma accumulated in lung and tracheobronchial lymph nodes, reduced airway hyper-reactivity and eosinophilic inflammation, and prevented excessive mucus, allergen-specific IgE and Th2 cytokine rises, outperforming non-modified Tregs—enabling therapy for severe allergic asthma. A third study estimates adverse consequences of unmet need among older dual-eligible versus Medicare-only beneficiaries.
